topics.title: 14. INVENTORY MANAGEMENT
explain: Inventory constitutes a major element of working capital, making proper investment control essential.
Its key objectives closely mirror those of cash management by balancing liquidity and cost control.
It covers fixing minimum/maximum stock levels and determining the economic order quantity (EOQ).
It includes managing receipts, issues, inspection, proper storage, movement control, and preventing obsolescence.
Detailed concepts are covered under Paper 4: Cost and Management Accounting (Chapter 2: Material Cost).

flow.title: Process of Inventory Management Control
steps: Fix minimum and maximum stock levels
Decide procedures for issue of stock

topics.example: A retail store sets fixed reorder levels for goods so it never runs out of stock or overspends on excess storage.
remember: Inventory management aims are similar to cash management objectives.
mistakes: Ignoring stock movement control, which can lead to unsellable obsolete inventory.

quiz.q: The objectives of inventory management are largely similar to the objectives of which other working capital component?
quiz.why: The text explicitly states that inventory management objectives are, to a great extent, similar to those of cash management.

quiz.q: Detailed study of Inventory Management is referred to which paper and chapter?
quiz.why: The text directs students to refer to Chapter 2 (Material Cost) of Paper 4: Cost and Management Accounting.
